resources.string: Paste here the token that @BotFather gave you. It is your bot’s “password”: with it the app can receive and answer messages.
All good! We found your bot.
Use another bot or a new token
I don’t have a token / how do I get one?
How to create a bot and get the token
The token stays only on this phone, stored encrypted. Nobody but you and Telegram can access it.

string-array.name: botfather_steps
string-array.item: Open Telegram and search for @BotFather (it has the blue verified badge).
Tap Start and send /newbot.
Choose a name for the bot (spaces are fine, e.g. Ann’s Shop).
Choose a username that ends in “bot” (e.g. annsshop_bot).
BotFather replies with the token: a line like 123456789:AAH… Tap it to copy.
Come back here, paste it in the field above and tap Check token.

string-array.name: botfather_token_steps
string-array.item: Open @BotFather in Telegram.
Send /mybots and pick your bot.
Tap API Token to see the current token (or Revoke to generate a new one).
Copy the whole token and paste it here again.

Warning: Android may shut the bot down when the screen is off. Tap to fix it.
Turns the bot on by itself when the phone is switched on or restarted
The bot runs on this phone: when it is off or without internet, the bot is offline. Telegram keeps messages for up to 24 hours and the bot answers the pending ones when it comes back.
Webhook removed. The bot will work again in a few seconds.
When someone sends the command to the bot, it replies with the text you wrote. Commands show up by themselves in Telegram’s “/” menu.

Persistent notification that keeps the bot running
To save battery, Android often closes apps that keep running with the screen off. Since the bot has to stay on all the time, do the two steps below once.
Without this, Android cuts the app’s internet when the screen turns off and the bot stops answering. Tap the button and choose “Allow”.
Done! The app is already free from battery optimization.
Many brands have their own power saver that closes apps even after step 1. Follow the steps:

string-array.name: guide_generic
string-array.item: Tap “Open app settings”.
Go to Battery (or Battery usage).
Choose “Unrestricted” (or “Don’t optimize”).
If there is an “Allow background activity” option, keep it on.

string-array.name: guide_xiaomi
string-array.item: Tap “Open app settings”.
Turn on “Autostart”.
Go to “Battery saver” and choose “No restrictions”.
Open recent apps, hold Easy Telebot and tap the lock to lock it.

string-array.name: guide_samsung
string-array.item: Tap “Open app settings”.
Go to Battery and choose “Unrestricted”.
In Settings › Battery › Background usage limits, make sure Easy Telebot is NOT in “Sleeping apps” or “Deep sleeping apps”.
If you can, add the app to “Never sleeping apps”.

string-array.name: guide_huawei
string-array.item: Go to Settings › Battery › App launch.
Find Easy Telebot and turn off “Manage automatically”.
In the window that opens, turn on all three options: auto-launch, secondary launch and run in background.
In recent apps, pull Easy Telebot down to lock it.

string-array.name: guide_oneplus
string-array.item: Tap “Open app settings”.
Go to Battery usage and choose “Unrestricted” (or “Don’t optimize”).
Turn on “Allow background activity” and “Auto-launch”, if they exist.
In recent apps, lock Easy Telebot (padlock icon).

string-array.name: guide_oppo
string-array.item: Tap “Open app settings”.
Go to Battery usage and turn on “Allow background activity” and “Allow auto-launch”.
In Settings › Battery, turn off optimization for Easy Telebot.
In recent apps, lock Easy Telebot (padlock icon).

string-array.name: guide_vivo
string-array.item: Go to Settings › Battery › Background power consumption.
Allow high background power consumption for Easy Telebot.
In i Manager › App manager › Autostart, turn on Easy Telebot.
In recent apps, lock Easy Telebot.

A token looks like 123456789:AAH… (numbers, a colon and a long run of letters). Make sure you copied the whole line, without spaces.
Telegram didn’t recognize this token. It may have been mistyped or changed (revoked) in @BotFather. Get the current token like this:

Telegram lets only one program at a time receive a bot’s messages, and another one is already doing it.

string-array.name: err_conflict_steps
string-array.item: Check whether the same bot is running on another phone or computer and turn it off there.
If you don’t recognize that other place, change the token in @BotFather (/mybots › API Token › Revoke) and paste the new one here.

resources.string: The bot is set up with a webhook
This bot was previously set up to send its messages to a server (webhook). While that is active, the app can’t receive them. Tap the button below to remove the webhook and use the bot here.
The chat ID is wrong or the bot is not part of that group/channel. Add the bot to the group and try again.
The bot can’t start a conversation
On Telegram, a bot can only message people who talked to it first. The person needs to open the bot and send /start.
This person blocked the bot, so it can no longer send them messages. Nothing to do on your side.
The bot has no permission in this group
The bot is not allowed to send messages in this group or channel.

string-array.name: err_rights_steps
string-array.item: Open the group/channel in Telegram and tap its name.
Go to Administrators › Add administrator and choose your bot.
Turn on the permission to send/post messages and save.

resources.string: Too many messages in a short time
Telegram asked the bot to wait a little before sending more messages. The app waits the requested time and continues by itself.
This shouldn’t happen. The rejected text was saved in the log; if you can, tell the developer and show that line.
The bot was on, but the system closed the app without you asking (usually to save battery). Free the app from battery saving so this doesn’t happen again.
Something went wrong and I didn’t recognize the problem. Try again; if it keeps happening, tell the developer with the detail below.
Paste the token of a bot created in @BotFather
You don’t have any bots yet. Tap “Add bot” to start.
This bot is already in the app. We’ll just update its token.
Shows the commands in Telegram’s “Menu” button and when the person types “/”. When off, the menu is empty.
Download the complete bot (.zip) to run on a computer or server and change it as you like
Deletes this bot, its commands and token from the app (the bot still exists on Telegram)
The bot will be turned off and its commands, media and token will be deleted from this phone. If you want to keep a copy, use “Export source code” first. The bot still exists on Telegram.
What do you want to add?
One or more commands (e.g. /start and /begin) that reply with one or more messages: formatted text, photos, videos, files and link buttons.
Coming soon: group moderation, support desk, AI and more.
Like a simple command, but only administrators of the chosen class (or higher) can use it. For everyone else, the bot doesn’t answer.
Creates a secret code so someone can become a bot admin through Telegram.

The .zip file contains the bot engine (the same Python code that runs here), your commands, the media and a run.py. To use it: unzip and run “python3 run.py” on any computer with Python 3.9+. Remember to turn the bot off on the phone first, since it can only run in one place at a time.
Include the token in the file
Whoever has this file will control your bot. Don’t share it with anyone.
Couldn’t save the file. Try choosing another folder.
Type and tap Add. You can have more than one, for example /start and /begin.
Appears in Telegram’s menu (uses the first command and the description)

Messages are sent in this order. Formatting: *bold*, _italic_, __underline__, ~strikethrough~, ||spoiler||, `code`, [text](link) and “> ” at the start of the line for a quote. The buttons above the text do this for you.
Captions go up to 1024 characters. The text will be sent in a separate message, right after the media.
Show preview of links in the text

Add at least one command (e.g. start).

string-array.name: botfather_photo_steps
string-array.item: Open @BotFather and send /setuserpic.
Choose this bot from the list.
Send the new photo (as a photo, not as a file).
Come back here and open the profile again to see the updated photo.

resources.string: This token belongs to another bot

The token you pasted belongs to another bot. To change this bot’s token, get its token in @BotFather (/mybots › choose the bot › API Token). If you want to add the other bot, use “Add bot” on the home screen.
Who can use admin commands, and in which class

Administrators have classes from I to X. Class I is the highest and can do everything. A class can use its own commands and those of the classes below: class III uses the commands of III, IV, V…, but not those of II and I. There can be as many admins as you want in each class.
Nobody yet. Tap “Add administrator” to generate a code.
Class I: the highest. Can use every admin command.
Class %1$s: uses the commands of classes %1$s to %2$s. Doesn’t use the commands of class %3$s.
To generate an administrator code for %1$s

For safety, administrators can only be created on a phone with a screen lock (PIN, pattern, password or fingerprint). That way, nobody who grabs your unlocked phone for a moment can become an admin of your bot.
The future admin must open the private chat with @%1$s and send exactly this message:
Copied! Paste it in the chat with the bot.
The bot is off. Turn it on so it can receive the code.
Don’t share this code in groups: whoever sends it first becomes admin. The bot ignores the command in groups. After it is used, the bot tries to delete the message with the code.
The person immediately loses access to admin commands. To come back, a new code must be generated.
Only admins can use it. For non-admins, the bot doesn’t answer (the command seems not to exist).
Only class I admins can use it.
Appears only in the menu of admins who can use it (in the private chat with the bot)
/%1$s is a command reserved by the app (used to add admins).
%1$s tried to use /%2$s, but is not an admin. Nothing was answered.
%1$s (class %3$s) tried to use /%2$s, which requires class %4$s. Nothing was answered.
%1$s sent /newadmin without a code. Nothing was answered.
%1$s sent /newadmin with an invalid or expired code. Nothing was answered.
%1$s sent /newadmin in a group. Ignored: it only works in a private chat.
Where the bot keeps users, history and backup: %1$s

The bot can keep who talked to it (the base for features like sending notices to everyone) and the message history. The database also keeps a backup of your commands and administrators, so you can recover the bot on another phone or on a computer.
Name, @username, ID, first and last time they talked to the bot and how many messages they sent
Every message received and sent by the bot (text, type, who sent it, where, whether it was an automatic reply or sent by you). Takes more space; tell your users that conversations are stored.
On this phone, in a folder only the app uses. Simple, no setup.
JSON files in a folder you can see in the file manager (/sdcard). Needs “all files access”.
Google/Firebase cloud database. Good free plan. Needs the database URL.
Cloud Firestore with a service account (.json file). Works with Firebase and Google Cloud projects.
Amazon’s database. Needs an access key; the app creates the table by itself.
The data stays in an internal app folder. Warning: if you uninstall the app or clear its data, it is deleted. Use a backup in a cloud database if you want to keep a copy.
To write outside the app folder, Android requires the “All files access” permission.
The data stays there even if you uninstall the app, and you can copy the folder to a computer. Other apps with file access can also read this folder.
The chosen file is not a Google service account JSON (it needs client_email, private_key and project_id).
Leave (default), unless you created another database in the project.
If it doesn’t exist, the app creates it when you tap Test (billed only by usage).
Connection working! The app wrote, read and deleted a test item.
Connection working! The table didn’t exist and was created.
Save the changes before using the backup or viewing the data.
The backup keeps this bot’s commands (with texts, buttons and settings) and administrators in the chosen database. Media files are not included.
This bot’s current commands and administrators will be replaced by the backup’s. Media files that are not on this phone will need to be attached again.
Backup from %1$s restored: %2$d command(s) and %3$d administrator(s).
Nobody yet. Users show up here after they message the bot while it’s on.

string-array.name: storage_firebase_steps
string-array.item: Go to console.firebase.google.com and create (or open) a project.
In the menu, go to Build › Realtime Database › Create database.
Copy the URL shown at the top (it ends in firebaseio.com or firebasedatabase.app) and paste it here.
Secret: Project settings (gear) › Service accounts › Database secrets › Show. Paste it in the “Database secret” field.
Without a secret, the database only works if its rules allow public access — not recommended.

string-array.name: storage_firestore_steps
string-array.item: In the Firebase (or Google Cloud) console, open the project and create the database in Firestore Database › Create database (native mode).
Go to Project settings › Service accounts › Generate new private key. A .json file will be downloaded.
On Google Cloud, the account needs the “Cloud Datastore User” role (or Editor). Accounts created by Firebase already have it.
Tap “Choose the service account .json file” and select the downloaded file. It is stored encrypted on this phone.

string-array.name: storage_aws_steps
string-array.item: In the AWS console, open IAM › Users › Create user (e.g. easytelebot).
Give it the AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess permission (or a policy just for the bot’s table).
In the created user, go to Security credentials › Create access key › “Application running outside AWS”.
Copy the key ID and the secret key into the fields above. AWS shows the secret key only once.
Choose the region and tap Test: if the table doesn’t exist, the app creates it.

resources.string: The database is not fully set up
Some database field is empty or in a format we don’t recognize. Check the data on the Database screen.
The credential (secret, service account or AWS key) is wrong, was revoked or has no permission for this database.

string-array.name: err_storage_auth_steps
string-array.item: Make sure you copied the whole credential, without spaces.
Firebase: check the database secret or the access rules.
Firestore: check the service account’s role and whether the Firestore API is enabled in the project.
AWS: check that the user has DynamoDB permission and that the key is active.

resources.string: The address, project, database or table given doesn’t exist (or wasn’t created yet).

string-array.name: err_storage_not_found_steps
string-array.item: Firebase: check the Realtime Database URL in the console.
Firestore: create the database in Firestore Database › Create database.
AWS: check the region; tap Test so the app creates the table.

Stickers that already appeared in the bot’s conversations. Or choose a .webp file (512×512).

Build the messages and choose who gets them. Texts accept formatting and variables: {name} becomes each person’s name.

The bot only knows people who already messaged it and the groups and channels it was added to (from this version on). Channels: add the bot as an administrator allowed to post. If it was already in the channel, remove it and add it again so the app finds it. People who blocked the bot leave the list by themselves.

Admins can build and send broadcasts right from Telegram, without opening the app

string-array.name: broadcast_how_steps
string-array.item: In the private chat with the bot, the admin sends /post (or /publi).
Sends the broadcast messages however they like: formatted text, photos, videos, documents, albums, stickers… The bot reacts with a “thumbs up” to each one.
Sends /pronto: the bot shows the preview exactly as it will arrive, how many recipients exist and a code.
Sends /confirmar CODE for everyone, or /confirmar CODE usuarios (or grupos, canais; they can be combined).
The bot sends it without showing who wrote it and, at the end, sends a summary. /cancelar gives up or stops the sending.

resources.string: Regular Telegram can’t send buttons, so write lines like these at the end of the text or caption: each line becomes a row of buttons and disappears from the text. A message with only these lines puts the buttons on the previous message (useful for a photo without a caption). Albums don’t accept buttons.
The bot can no longer reach this chat
The bot was removed from the group/channel, isn’t allowed to post there, or the person’s account was deleted.
Write a text or attach media in at least one message.
There are no users, groups or channels of the chosen type. They show up when they talk to the bot or when the bot is added to a group or channel.
A broadcast is already being sent
Wait for the current broadcast to finish (or stop it) before starting another.

Anyone who sends too many messages in a short time, or repeats the same message several times, is blocked right away: the bot starts ignoring the person. You and the admins are notified and decide whether to unblock or keep the block. Admins are never blocked.
When off, nobody is blocked automatically (existing blocks still apply).
Blocks with more than 15 messages in 10 seconds or the same message 6 times in 1 minute. For very busy bots.
Blocks with more than 8 messages in 10 seconds or the same message 4 times in 1 minute. Recommended.
Blocks with more than 5 messages in 10 seconds or the same message 3 times in 1 minute. May catch people in a hurry; keep an eye on the notices.
They get: “You were blocked automatically… An administrator will review the case.” If unblocked, they are also notified.
Who gets the notice and can decide on Telegram

On Telegram, each admin gets the case with the reason, the latest messages and the Unblock and Keep blocked buttons. One admin’s decision shows up for everyone and here in the app. In groups, only commands sent to the bot count (normal chatting doesn’t). A photo album counts as a single message, and repeating the same command (e.g. /start) doesn’t count as a repeated message.
The bot answers the person again, and they get a notice that they were unblocked. The admins’ notices on Telegram are updated.
The bot answers the person again. The admins’ notices on Telegram are updated.
On: blocks whoever floods the bot
The bot will ignore everything this person sends (no command answers). Their messages still show up here. You can unblock whenever you want, here or on the Antispam screen.
Blocked: the bot is ignoring this person
Antispam blocks waiting for your review.
%1$s was blocked automatically (%2$s). Tap to review and decide.
Something to sell: a file, course, link, code… Delivery is automatic after payment.
Paid access to a channel or group for a period. The bot invites, reminds people to renew and removes those who didn’t.
The shop is off: the bot doesn’t show the products. Tap to turn it on and set up payments.
No products yet. Create the first one below.
No orders yet. They show up here as soon as someone buys through the bot.
The person leaves %1$s now and is notified. They can come back by subscribing again.
The bot answers /loja with the catalog and sells through the payments set up below.
Use your Mercado Pago account’s currency (Brazil = BRL). Bitcoin is converted on the spot using Blink’s rate.
Payment link with Pix, card and boleto, or Pix with a QR code in the chat.
On the Mercado Pago site: Your business, Settings, Your integrations (or mercadopago.com/developers), create an application and copy the production Access Token.
Pix with a QR code in the chat
The bot sends the QR code and the copy-and-paste code right in the chat. Mercado Pago requires a payer e-mail: use one of yours.
The bot creates a Lightning invoice for the order amount, converted at the current rate, and checks by itself when it’s paid.
At dashboard.blink.sv, sign in with your Blink account, open API Keys and create a key with Read and Receive permissions. Don’t check the sending one (Write).
Telegram’s native payment, no sign-up. Only shows for products priced in stars. For digital goods sold inside Telegram, Telegram’s rules require Stars.
Credentials are stored encrypted on the phone and only used to talk to Mercado Pago and Blink. When you save, the bot restarts if it’s on.
Besides the list in the chat, the bot shows a button that opens the storefront with photos, cart and quantities, right inside Telegram.

The storefront is a fixed page (docs/loja in the app repository) that gets the catalog through the link itself: no server needed. Use the default address or host the page wherever you like (it must be https).
Who gets the notice of each sale on Telegram

resources.string: Something unexpected happened in the shop. The details are below.
Commands in any programming language and a local API for bot libraries
The command runs a program of yours in Termux (Python, Node, Bash, Ruby…) and replies with what it prints.
Termux is a Linux terminal for Android. With it, the bot does whatever you program: query sites and APIs, use databases, generate images, automate the phone… In any language.

string-array.name: termux_install_steps
string-array.item: Install Termux from F-Droid or from the official GitHub (termux/termux-app). The old Play Store version won’t work.
Open Termux once and wait for the setup to finish.
Install the language you want, for example: pkg install python nodejs

resources.string: Allow other apps to use Termux
For safety, Termux only accepts commands from other apps after you allow it. Paste this command in Termux once:

string-array.name: termux_external_steps
string-array.item: Open Termux and paste: echo \"allow-external-apps = true\" >> ~/.termux/termux.properties
Then run: termux-reload-settings (or close and open Termux).
Check in Termux and scripts that the “Run commands in Termux” permission is granted and tap Test.
If Android is saving Termux’s battery, free it: Settings, Apps, Termux, Battery, Unrestricted.

resources.string: Permission to run commands in Termux granted
Missing the permission to run commands in Termux
If Android doesn’t show the request: Settings, Apps, Easy Telebot, Permissions, Additional permissions, Run commands in Termux.
Create a command and choose Reply with: Termux script. When someone uses the command, the app runs your command line in Termux and sends what the program prints.

string-array.name: termux_env_vars

string-array.item: Plain text: becomes a message, with the same formatting as commands (*bold*, _italic_, [link](site.com)).

A button with \"data\" runs the same script again with TELEBOT_DATA. With \"edit\": true, the reply edits the button’s message.
\"html\": true sends the text as Telegram HTML, without conversion.
Nothing printed: no reply. An error (exit code other than 0) shows up in the bot log with the end of stderr.
